### F-120 — `NoSuchBucket` after a cluster restart was an ephemeral MinIO volume

> _2026-09-10 · test/blong-int-adapter · resolved_

`test/blong-int-adapter/s3.test.ts` failed with `NoSuchBucket` for `blong-integration` while the
terminal showed only `Alarm clock` and exit 142. Neither the test nor the restructure was at fault:
`minio-deployment.yaml` declares no `volumeMounts` and no `persistentVolumeClaim`, so `/data` is
container-ephemeral (mysql, mongodb and keycloak do have PVCs). The k3d cluster had restarted, the
MinIO container had died uncleanly (Exit 255, Reason `Unknown`) and came back with an empty `/data`
holding only `.minio.sys`, and the one-shot `minio-bucket-init` Job was still `Complete` from 2d19h
earlier, so nothing recreated the bucket.

Re-running the documented init job fixed it and the suite passed 15/15: delete the
`minio-bucket-init` Job in the `blong-integration` namespace, then
`kubectl apply -k test/integration/`.

Exit 142 is SIGALRM, not a process error: here the harness timeout fired because the first failing
group left `Watch: operation "run test groups" still running (progress 1/3)` hanging, which buried
the real error. When an integration test fails right after a cluster restart, check the backend's
data (`kubectl exec deploy/minio -- ls /data`) before suspecting the test.

### F-121 — The Kafka seed Job needed a message probe, not a topic probe

> _2026-09-10 · test/blong-int-adapter · resolved_

Making the seed Job idempotent took three attempts. Guarding on the question 'does the topic exist?'
looks right and silently skips re-seeding after a reboot: `kafka-deployment.yaml` has a
`lifecycle.postStart` hook running `kafka-topics --create --if-not-exists`, so every container start
recreates an empty topic, and the topic exists while the seed message is gone. The guard has to test
for the message.

Probing with `kafka-console-consumer --from-beginning --timeout-ms 3000` reported zero messages even
though messages were there: it exited with `TimeoutException`, because `--timeout-ms` maps to the
request timeout and a group-based consumer must first wait out the broker's
`group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms` (3000 ms by default), so the probe looked like 'no seed' and
seeded a duplicate on every run.

`kafka-console-consumer --partition 0 --offset 0` reads the partition directly with no consumer
group, and is therefore fast and deterministic; that is the form the Job uses now. Verified both
ways: after `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kafka` (an empty topic, the real post-reboot state)
the Job seeds exactly one message, and a second run logs 'Seed message already present' with the
count still 1.
